title: Reverie Interrompue
identity: The Philharmonie de Paris guide describes Dautremer’s Rêverie interrompue as a complete 1954 work for alto saxophone and piano, in two connected 4/4 sections, first slow and peaceful and then faster, with both slurred and detached articulation. It lists duration as four minutes. Windmusic’s library record adds AL21352, score and part pagination, and a pedagogical repertory year descriptor.

evidence.claim: Guide gives 1954 date, two connected 4/4 parts, contrast, articulation and complete-piece performance context.
evidence.source_name: Philharmonie de Paris, 10 ans avec le saxophone

evidence.claim: Windmusic library record confirms Leduc AL21352, 1954, 4-page score plus part, four-minute duration and its own pedagogical descriptor.
Quebec conservatory syllabus places the work among simple, songful repertoire selections for tone study.
evidence.source_name: Conservatoire de musique et d’art dramatique du Québec

review_focus: Inference: the documented shift from slow, peaceful writing to a faster section with mixed slurred and detached articulation makes phrasing and contrast concrete review points.
collection_flag: Pedagogical repertoire with documented conservatory syllabus use; not enough evidence to claim a simplified transcription.

score_links.description: Pedagogical guide, PDF page 40 / printed page 43

gaps: The guide describes “justesse et musicalité” but does not specify written/sounding pitch range.
